Usually, works of literature don't openly state their themes. But you can often identify themes by looking at important moments in the text, including dialogue, action, and observations made by the narrator.

text.text: In 2004, when Rolling Stone magazine published its list of the "500 Greatest Songs of All Time," it included one tune written entirely in Spanish.
Called "La Bamba," the song was recorded in 1958 by teenage musician Ritchie Valens.
<atomic>The original "La Bamba" is an eighteenth-century Mexican folk song mainly performed at weddings.</atomic>
Valens decided to record the song using a more upbeat rock tempo.
<atomic>The result was the first Top 40 hit for a Spanish-language song in the United States.</atomic>
Similarly, the 1984 song "99 Luftballons" was one of the first German-language songs to become a hit in the U.S.
While there is no direct English translation of the term "La Bamba," it likely comes from the Spanish word bambolear, meaning "to sway," making it a fitting title for this dance-worthy ditty.

contents.text: When you write a paragraph, it should focus on a topic. For example, maybe your paragraph is about the tallest mountains in Colorado. Each sentence should give information that helps develop the topic:

Colorado is home to fifty-eight mountains that rise fourteen thousand feet or higher above sea level. These majestic peaks, proudly known as the 14ers, offer many opportunities for outdoor exploration. They are popular destinations for hikers, rock climbers, and skiers. Stargazers also seek out these isolated mountaintops as places to search the sky. Likewise, many adventurers flock to the 14ers to watch the uniquely adapted wildlife that thrives at these extreme elevations.
If a sentence does not help develop the topic, it should not appear in the paragraph.

contents.text: In 2004, when Rolling Stone magazine published its list of the "500 Greatest Songs of All Time," it included one tune written entirely in Spanish. header.text: When writing, make sure to avoid vague pronoun references. A vague pronoun reference occurs when a pronoun could refer to more than one possible antecedent.

sentences.text: When Lisa and Kim finally landed, she breathed a sigh of relief.
The pronoun she could refer to either Lisa or Kim, so the meaning of the sentence is unclear.

header.text: Vague pronoun references can be corrected in one of two ways:

sentences.text: 1. Replace the pronoun with its correct antecedent:
When Lisa and Kim finally landed, Lisa breathed a sigh of relief.
2. Rewrite the sentence:
Lisa breathed a sigh of relief when she and Kim finally landed.

header.text: A vague pronoun reference also occurs when they, them, their, theirs, it, or its is used without its antecedent.

sentences.text: They say that this nail polish dries in less than five minutes.
The pronoun they is used without its antecedent, so the meaning of the sentence is unclear.

header.text: This problem can be fixed by replacing the pronoun with its missing antecedent.
